faqSection.title: Questions About Studying in United Kingdom
faqSection.description: Find answers to common questions regarding admissions, English tests, visa requirements, and student life in United Kingdom.

faqs.question: Can I study in the United Kingdom without IELTS?
faqs.answer: Yes, some universities accept alternative English qualifications such as PTE Academic, Duolingo or other approved tests. Some institutions may also accept a Medium of Instruction certificate, subject to their admission requirements.

faqs.question: How long can I stay after completing my graduation?
faqs.answer: Post-study work opportunities depend on the applicable immigration route, your qualification and the rules in force when you apply. Check the current official immigration requirements before making plans.

faqs.question: Can international students work part-time while studying?
faqs.answer: Work permissions depend on your visa conditions and course. Check the work restrictions stated on your immigration permission before accepting employment.

faqs.question: What are the main university academic intakes?
faqs.answer: Many universities offer September and January intakes. Some institutions also offer additional intakes depending on the programme and availability.

faqs.question: What is a CAS letter?
faqs.answer: A Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) is an electronic reference issued by an eligible UK university sponsor. It is used as part of the Student visa application process.

faqs.question: How much money do I need to show for my student visa?
faqs.answer: Financial evidence requirements depend on tuition fees, study location and the current immigration rules. Check the official UK government guidance for the latest maintenance funds and holding-period requirements.

faqSection.title: Questions About Studying in Australia
faqSection.description: Find answers to common questions about Australian university admissions, English tests, student visas, part-time work and living costs.

faqs.question: Can I study in Australia without IELTS?
faqs.answer: IELTS is not the only English language test accepted by Australian universities. Many institutions accept alternatives such as PTE Academic, TOEFL iBT, OIETC and Cambridge English, depending on their admission policies. Duolingo is not universally accepted, so students should check the specific university requirements.

faqs.question: How long can I stay in Australia after completing my studies?
faqs.answer: Eligible international graduates may apply for the Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485), under the Post-Higher Education Work stream. The source lists general periods of 2 years for Bachelor's degrees, up to 4 years for Master's by Coursework, up to 2 years for Master's by Research, and up to 4 years for doctoral degrees. Applicants must meet the relevant age, qualification and visa requirements.

faqs.question: Can international students work part-time while studying in Australia?
faqs.answer: International students holding a valid Student Visa (subclass 500) can generally work up to 48 hours per fortnight while their course is in session. During official course breaks, they can work unlimited hours, subject to visa conditions. Different entitlements may apply to Master's by Research and doctoral students.

faqs.question: What are the main university intakes in Australia?
faqs.answer: Australian universities generally offer February/March and July intakes. Some universities also offer additional intakes in November or other months, depending on the course and availability.

faqs.question: What is a Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE), and when do I receive it?
faqs.answer: A Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE) is an official electronic document issued by an Australian education provider after you accept your admission offer and complete the required enrolment steps. In most cases, students must accept the offer, pay the required tuition fee deposit and arrange OSHC before receiving the CoE. It is required for an Australian Student Visa (subclass 500) application.

faqs.question: How much money do I need to show for an Australian student visa?
faqs.answer: Students must demonstrate sufficient funds for tuition fees, living expenses, OSHC and travel costs. The source lists AUD 29,710 for 12 months of living expenses for a single student, in addition to first-year tuition, OSHC and travel expenses. Financial evidence may include bank deposits, scholarships or acceptable financial sponsorship.

faqs.question: Can I bring my spouse or family members to Australia?
faqs.answer: The supplied content states that, under Australian Student Visa rules effective from 2 October 2026, most international students can no longer include a spouse or dependent children in their Student Visa (subclass 500) application or generally bring them later as subsequent entrants. It lists limited exemptions for certain PhD students, DFAT or Defence-sponsored students, eligible foreign-government scholarship recipients, and eligible nationals of certain Pacific Island or ASEAN countries. Bangladesh is not included in the Pacific Island or ASEAN exemption. Check the latest Department of Home Affairs requirements before making plans.
